source: records lifted verbatim out of real transcripts under ~/.claude/projects on the machine this was assembled on, not synthesised and not produced by capture-traces.ts (which has never captured claude). Only the fields that identify a person's conversation were rewritten: cwd, sessionId, timestamp, and the sidechain/request ids. Every `content` string is byte-for-byte what the CLI wrote, escape sequences included.
why: the two defects a person hit: a slash command rendered as the words "Local command", twice, and `"model": "<synthetic>"` adopted as the session's model. Both are shapes no hand-written fixture in this repo had ever seen.

records.shape: system/local_command, content is the raw text the person typed ("/status") with no tags at all
records.note: this is the exact record sedano itself produced when the user reported the bug — entrypoint sdk-cli is this app
the second half of the same pair: together these two records are the two "Local command" lines

records.shape: system/local_command, content is <command-name>/<command-message>/<command-args>, indented by the CLI's own template
system/local_command stdout carrying real terminal escapes (ESC[1m … ESC[22m)
records.note: proves stripAnsi is answering real bytes rather than a hypothesis

records.shape: type user, message.content a plain string carrying the same command tags
records.note: still emitted by current CLIs; the `user` branch reads message.content as an array, so this shape rendered as nothing at all

records.shape: the same user shape with <command-args></command-args> empty
type assistant whose message.model is the literal string <synthetic>, stop_reason stop_sequence, an all-zero usage block, and isApiErrorMessage/apiErrorStatus/quotaLimits alongside
records.note: the text is a rate-limit notice the CLI wrote itself. The all-zero usage is what normalizeUsage must keep refusing: no model ran, so no tokens were spent and none may be claimed.
